existingFloorArea.reason: Remaining floor area is measured against PLUTO gross building area.

zfaVsGfaGuidance.note: PLUTO `bldgarea` is Department of Finance gross building area (GFA), NOT Department of Buildings zoning floor area (ZFA) under ZR 12-10 (which excludes qualifying cellar space, mechanical/electrical/HVAC space, accessory parking up to statutory caps, and exterior wall-thickness deductions, often making ZFA 85%–95% of GFA). In your headline and prose, explicitly separate PLUTO GFA from DOB ZFA, show the 100% / 95% / 90% / 85% ZFA sensitivity band and floor-equivalent conversions when relevant, and state that an architect’s DOB ZD1/PW1/Certificate of Occupancy audit is required to establish true unused ZFA.

scenarios.name: As-of-right development
conditions: Complies with district bulk, height, yard and parking rules as modeled in the zoning envelope.

scenarios.name: Universal Affordability Preference (qualifying affordable housing)
conditions: Residential FAR may exceed the standard table (4 FAR = 20000 sq ft) up to the qualifying-affordable FAR (5.01 FAR = 25050 sq ft) — the 5050 sq ft bonus (20.2% of total residential ZFA) is matched 1:1 by permanently income-restricted floor area averaging <=60% AMI under an HPD regulatory agreement and permit notice (ZR 27-111, ZR 27-131).
Applies outside Mandatory Inclusionary Housing areas; inside them MIH governs instead.
Heights may also rise to the qualifying-affordable rows of ZR 23-432.

scenarios.name: BSA variance
conditions: All five ZR 72-21 findings are mandatory: (a) unique physical conditions inherent in the lot causing practical difficulties or unnecessary hardship; (b) no reasonable return from a conforming development (waived for non-profits); (c) no alteration of the neighborhood’s essential character or detriment to adjacent property/public welfare; (d) hardship not self-created; (e) the minimum variance necessary.
Needs a feasibility study for finding (b) in most use/bulk cases and survives Article 78 challenge risk after approval.

conditions: Needed for map changes beyond the ELURP limits (more than 30% added maximum residential floor area, a new non-horizontal height plane, or more than 2 FAR of newly permitted commercial floor area), for actions needing an EIS outside Fast Track, and for special permits.
Pre-certification and environmental review (CEQR) precede the ULURP clock: community board and borough president advisory votes, then binding CPC and City Council votes.

If the Council disapproves or modifies a single-borough application that facilitates affordable housing, the Affordable Housing Appeals Board (Mayor, Council Speaker and Borough President) may reverse it on a request filed within 5 days, deciding within 15 days.

Affordable Housing Fast Track (Charter §197-f) can move publicly funded affordable projects citywide, and affordable housing in the 12 community districts that have permitted the least affordable housing, into expedited review ending at the City Planning Commission, even when an EIS is required (the Commission then has 45 days). Eligibility follows the Commission’s Fast Track methodology; confirm the current district list and criteria before relying on it.

Rezonings that increase residential capacity are generally paired with mapping a Mandatory Inclusionary Housing area (MIH, ZR 27-131), whose requirements are shares of residential floor area: Option 1 requires 25% permanently affordable at an average of 60% AMI (with 10% at 40% AMI); Option 2 requires 30% at an average of 80% AMI.
Precedent strength should be researched from CPC reports and dispositions and nearby ULURP actions before this path is priced.

elurpSteps: 1. Pre-Application & Environmental Review (same pre-certification and certification standards as ULURP; actions needing an EIS are excluded unless they qualify for Affordable Housing Fast Track)
2. DCP Certification of Complete Application (starts the 90-day ELURP clock under NYC Charter §197-e)
3. Community Board and Borough President Review (concurrent, 60 days, advisory; longer for June and early-July certifications)
4. City Planning Commission Hearing & Vote (30 days, 45 for Fast Track applications with an EIS; the Commission’s decision is final, with no City Council review)
ulurpSteps: 1. Pre-Application & CEQR Environmental Review (EAS/EIS scoping, typically 9–18+ months before certification)
2. DCP Certification of Complete Application (starts the ~7-month statutory ULURP clock under NYC Charter §197-c)
3. Community Board Review (60 days, advisory recommendation)
4. Borough President & Borough Board Review (30 days, advisory recommendation)
5. City Planning Commission (CPC) Hearing & Vote (60 days, binding approval/modification)

6. City Council Review & Vote (50 days, binding vote and local Council Member deference; the Affordable Housing Appeals Board can reverse a disapproval or modification of a single-borough affordable housing application)

value.scoringNote: Feasibility scores rank paths by approval certainty less typical time (as-of-right 85, certification 70, authorization 60, ELURP 45, special permit 40, variance 25, ULURP 15; minus up to 25 for duration). They ignore price, politics and precedent — research those in the same answer and do not present a score as a probability.
value.note: Quantified scenarios are arithmetic from the curated FAR tables and the areas supplied; transfers and mergers are negotiated transactions, and every discretionary path needs its own findings. Starting points to verify, not entitlement determinations.

value.name: As-of-right rental
derivation: Interest carry = 7.25% × 2.5 years × 65% × (land $3,100,000 + half of construction $6,313,500) = $1,109,028
One bedroom rent = 15 × 550 sq ft × $6/sq ft/month × 12 = $554,400
Two bedroom rent = 8 × 800 sq ft × $5/sq ft/month × 12 = $391,680
Yield on cost = NOI $919,836 ÷ total development cost $16,836,028 = 5.46%
Unlevered return on cost = $2,528,940 ÷ $16,836,028 = 15.02%; levered return on equity = $2,528,940 ÷ $5,504,450 = 45.94%
Cash on cash = (NOI $919,836 − interest-only debt service $821,539) ÷ equity $5,504,450 = 1.79%

decision.label: As-of-right rental
decision.verdict: As-of-right rental supports the $3,100,000 land price at a 12% return on cost; it justifies up to $3,506,260, and rents and prices could fall 2% before it misses.

value.rubric: Rank by profit after incremental approval land carry. Approval months explicitly included in financing.termMonths are not charged again. Missing approval timelines leave that carry unpriced; the ranking is provisional. Entitlement score is an ordinal index rather than an actuarial probability and never multiplies dollars. Downside applies the same 10% rent/price shock to the leading program alone, keeping alternatives at base and deducting the same incremental carry; the joint downside shocks every program at once (rents and prices 10% lower, hard and soft cost 10% higher, cap rate 50 bps higher where there is income) and reports when that changes the leader. The decision is made on the recommended program: the highest land price that earns the target return on cost after carry, and the uniform rent and price change the stated land price needs.
value.note: Every figure is the pro forma model’s arithmetic on the shared inputs and each variant’s scaling; rents and prices carry their recorded sources. Affordable variants blend restricted and market rents across the same unit mix, a first-pass approximation, not an HPD term sheet. Each variant's taxBasis states the taxes it carries: a 485-x exemption, taxes stated for that variant, or the shared taxes.
